biography:
Steve Hogarth, also known as h, is an English singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist best known as the lead vocalist of the progressive rock band Marillion since 1989. Born Ronald Stephen Hoggarth in Kendal, England, he first worked as a keyboard player and co-lead vocalist with The Europeans and later sang with How We Live before joining Marillion after the departure of Fish.

Hogarth became a defining voice in Marillion’s later career, contributing additional keyboards and guitar as well as his distinctive emotive vocals and reflective lyrics. His first album with the band, Seasons End (1989), helped establish the Hogarth-era sound, and he has remained central to the group’s evolution within progressive rock.

Outside Marillion, Hogarth has pursued solo and collaborative work, including the 1997 solo release Ice Cream Genius issued under the name h. He is widely regarded for his expressive stage presence, poetic writing, and ability to bring emotional depth to modern progressive rock.
